title: Sports Team
story: Your local football league needs player profiles. Each player has a name, jersey number, and position. Before a game, the announcer reads each player's intro: "Number 10, playing Forward — Alex!"
why: Grouping related fields into a struct keeps player data organized and easy to pass to formatting functions.
analogy: A team is like a folder, the star player is a file inside it, and the fields are the file's contents. You open the folder first (`team`), then the file (`star`), then read a line (`name`).
try_it: Add a `substitute` method to Player that changes the name and number. Create a starting lineup of 5 players (use separate variables, no collections yet). Write a function that finds the player with the highest jersey number among any 3 given players.
tips: Build data from the inside out: create Players first, then the Team that contains them
Use `+` to concatenate strings with numbers — XIOM converts numbers to strings automatically
Dot notation chains left to right: `team.star.name` reads as (team's star's name)
common_mistakes: Trying to access `team.name` when you meant `team.star.name` — the star's name is nested one level deeper
Using `==` on strings from different sources — string comparison is case-sensitive
